testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What happens if you do not drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air builds up in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water stays in the tanks, it can freeze in cold weather and stop the brakes from working.

questions.question: You are driving at 55 mph on dry pavement and brake hard. How much extra distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception, reaction, brake lag, and braking. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, air brake leakage should not exceed ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test, air should leak no more than 2 psi per minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: When is an alcohol evaporator most important?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator adds alcohol to the brake system. This stops ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, what does it do?

options.text: It pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
It pushes the brake shoes against the brake linings.
It pushes the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do with the parking brake when leaving your vehicle?

options.text: Use it only if parked on a slope.
Do not use it because it damages the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. Do not use it if your brakes are very hot or wet with freezing temperatures.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: If you pump the brake pedal too much, air leaves the system faster than the compressor can replace it. The brakes may stop working if pressure drops too low.

questions.question: What happens if brakes get too hot?
questions.explanation: Brakes can handle a lot of heat, but too much heat causes brake fade. This means brakes lose power to slow the vehicle. Use engine braking to help slow down and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What should a driver do when leaving a vehicle unattended?

options.text: Set the parking brake only if parked on a slope.
Let air out of the tires by 10 percent.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What color light shows that ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: A yellow light on the dashboard alerts you that the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working.

questions.question: How many axles must have ABS for it to work on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: ABS on even one axle gives you better braking control than having no ABS at all.

questions.question: What should air tank drains be used for?

options.text: Only use them when it is wet outside

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from the tanks. Always drain the tanks completely when using the drain.

questions.question: When using spring brakes with a heavy load, how long will it take to stop?

options.text: It will be impossible to stop
It will take a long time
It will take a short time

questions.correctAnswerText: It will take a long time
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. When they activate, your vehicle needs more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: When should you not use the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot
When the brakes are very cold
When there is snow on the ground

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if your brakes are hot. Let them cool first to avoid damage.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes
How much air pressure is available
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes
questions.explanation: This gauge shows the air pressure being applied to the brakes. It helps you know if your brakes are fading.

questions.question: What should you never do when spring brakes are on?
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force could damage the brakes.

questions.question: What is the largest crack allowed in a brake drum?

options.text: One half the width of the friction area
One third the width of the friction area
One fifth the width of the friction area

questions.correctAnswerText: One half the width of the friction area
questions.explanation: Check your brake drums before each trip. Do not drive if any drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: When should the low air pressure warning activate?
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning must activate when tank pressure drops below 60 psi. The warning may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do at 125 psi?

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air
Begin pumping air into the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air
questions.explanation: At around 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your air tanks?
questions.explanation: The supply pressure gauge tells you how much air pressure is in each of your air tanks.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the driver should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving to ensure fuel reaches the engine.
Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
Begin driving right after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems. Watch the air pressure gauges to check the pressure levels.

questions.question: The rods in S-cam brakes move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. The driver adds this air pressure by:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: A ____ allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:
questions.explanation: To check slack adjusters, park on level ground, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to make sure it does not move more than about one inch from where the push rod attaches. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.
